definition: Serving a fast streaming first pass for live captions, then rescoring its n-best hypotheses or lattices (the compact graph of alternative transcriptions) with a stronger model or LLM for the final transcript.
details: Serving a fast streaming first pass for live captions, then rescoring its n-best hypotheses or lattices (the compact graph of alternative transcriptions) with a stronger model or LLM for the final transcript. The production pattern that reconciles low latency with best accuracy.

explainer.lead: Two-pass ASR serves a fast streaming first pass for live captions, then rescoring its n-best hypotheses or lattices with a stronger model or LLM for the final transcript. It matters as the production pattern reconciling low latency with best accuracy.

tiers.eli5: It gives you quick rough captions right away, then a slower, smarter pass fixes them up.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use the first pass for responsiveness and the second for accuracy, aligning the two outputs. A pitfall is latency and revision churn when the second pass changes text already shown.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, pass one produces an n-best list or lattice from a streaming acoustic model; pass two rescoring re-ranks those candidates with a stronger model or LLM. Limit: the final transcript cannot exceed the quality of candidates in the lattice.

explainer.example: Live captions appear within a fraction of a second, then the sentence is re-scored and corrected once the stronger model runs.
